digest.component_or_area: workflow step registration and size guards
propositions: No headroom guard exists on workflow_ops.py (794 LOC) and config.py (793 LOC), which exceed the 700-line policy threshold and are not covered by existing seam tests.

The assertion message in test_gate_dispatch_seam.py justifies a guard on gate_dispatch.py by claiming it holds three finalize_verdict call sites, but all five sites have been relocated to plan_review_recovery.py and plan_review/workflow_ops.py, leaving the assertion's premise stale.

A missed registration import (deletion of prerequisite_workflow_ops import at workflow_ops.py:45) is invisible to existing validation layers (schema, linter, test_contracts.py registry iteration) and only caught at runtime, with no static guard currently preventing silent unregistration.

Step registration depends entirely on import side effects to a process-global STEP_REGISTRY dict, making membership invisible to workflow schema validation and gate-YAML resolution checks unless isolated in a subprocess with clean sys.modules.

In-process assertions of registry membership are masked by prior test imports that pre-populate STEP_REGISTRY before the guard runs, making them unable to detect the defect they exist for unless run in subprocess isolation on a first import.
